items.prompt: Which force do you use to open a drawer?

options.why: You push to close a drawer. Opening it needs a pull.
Anything that starts to move needs a force.
Your hand moves the drawer, not a magnet.

hints: Think about which way the drawer moves.
Does the drawer move towards you or away from you?
Moving something towards you is one kind of force.
items.explanation: To open a drawer, you pull it towards you. A pull is a force.

items.prompt: What is friction?

options.text: a force that pulls things down to the ground
options.why: That is gravity, a different force.

options.text: a force made only by magnets
options.why: Magnets make magnetic forces. Friction comes from surfaces rubbing.

options.text: a force between two surfaces that slows movement

options.why: Friction is a force, not light.

hints: Think about rubbing your hands together.
Friction happens when surfaces touch and slide.
Does friction help things move or slow them down?
items.explanation: Friction is a force between two surfaces that rub together. It acts against movement and slows things down.

items.prompt: A toy car rolls down a ramp onto different surfaces. On which surface was friction greatest?

figure.alt: Bar chart of distance travelled: carpet 60 cm, wood 150 cm, tiles 190 cm, sandpaper 30 cm.

options.why: The car went furthest on tiles, so friction was smallest there.
The car went 60 cm on carpet. It stopped even sooner on another surface.
The car went 150 cm on wood, so friction was quite small.

hints: More friction slows the car down sooner.
So the surface with most friction gives the shortest distance.
items.explanation: The car stopped soonest on sandpaper, after only 30 cm. Rough sandpaper gave the most friction.

items.prompt: How much further did the car travel on tiles than on carpet?

figure.alt: Bar chart of distance travelled: carpet 60 cm, wood 150 cm, tiles 190 cm, sandpaper 30 cm.

hints: Find the bars for tiles and carpet.
How much further means find the difference.
Take the carpet distance away from the tiles distance.
items.explanation: The car went 190 cm on tiles and 60 cm on carpet. 190 take away 60 is 130 cm.

items.prompt: After mopping, a shop puts out a Wet floor sign. Why is a wet floor slippery?

options.text: Water reduces the friction between shoes and the floor.

options.why: Water does not push your feet. It makes the floor slippery.
A little water hardly changes the weight of your shoes.
Water makes the surface slippery, so there is less friction.

hints: Slippery means it is easy to slide.
Sliding is easier when friction is small.
Does water make friction bigger or smaller?
items.explanation: Water makes a thin slippery layer between shoes and the floor. This reduces friction, so feet can slide.

items.prompt: Choose 2 examples where friction is useful.

options.text: bike brakes rubbing on the wheels to stop
oil helping a bike chain move smoothly
options.why: Oil reduces friction. Here we want less friction, not more.

options.text: a child sliding fast down a smooth slide
options.why: Here the fun comes from small friction.
Skaters glide because there is very little friction.

hints: Useful friction helps you grip or stop.
Think about times when you do not want to slip.
Cross out examples where sliding is the aim.
items.explanation: Brakes use friction to slow a bike down, and shoe soles use friction to grip. In the other examples, people want less friction.

items.prompt: Choose 3 things a force can do.

options.why: Pushing or pulling does not change colour.
A force cannot change one material into another.

hints: Think about kicking a ball, catching it and squashing it.
Forces can also squash or stretch.
items.explanation: Forces can start or stop movement, speed things up, slow them down and change direction. They can also change shape by squashing, bending or stretching.

items.prompt: Sita pulls a brick across carpet with a forcemeter. It reads 6 N. On a smooth table it reads 2 N. Why?

options.text: The brick is lighter on the table.
options.why: The brick has not changed. Only the surface changed.

options.text: There is less friction on the smooth table.

options.why: The readings make sense: different surfaces give different friction.
The carpet needed the most force, so it has the most friction.

hints: The same brick was used both times.
What changed between the two pulls?
A bigger reading means more force was needed.
items.explanation: Smooth surfaces give less friction than rough ones. Less force was needed on the table, so the reading was smaller.

items.prompt: Forces are measured in units called ___.
hints: The unit is named after a famous scientist.
We use a forcemeter to measure it.
Its symbol is a capital N.
items.explanation: Forces are measured in newtons (N). A forcemeter measures force.

items.prompt: Why does a parachute fall slowly?

options.why: A parachute with a person is heavy. Air resistance slows it.
Gravity still pulls it down. Air pushes up against it.

options.text: Air pushes up against its big surface.

options.why: Parachutes slow down even when there is no wind.

hints: Think about the shape of a parachute.
Air resistance is a kind of friction with the air.
What does a big surface catch as it falls?
items.explanation: A parachute has a big surface that pushes against lots of air. This air resistance slows the fall.

items.prompt: Order the surfaces from most friction to least friction.
hints: Think about which surface would be hardest to slide on.
items.explanation: Sandpaper is roughest, so it has most friction. Ice is smoothest and most slippery, so it has least.

items.prompt: Car tyres have deep grooves. How do the grooves help on a wet road?

options.why: Grooves remove only a little rubber. Weight is not the reason.

options.text: They reduce friction so the car goes faster.
options.why: On wet roads we need more grip, not less.

options.text: They make the tyres look nicer.
options.why: Grooves have a real job to do.

options.text: They let water escape so the rubber can grip the road.

hints: On a wet road, water can get between the tyre and the road.
Where could the water go if there were channels in the tyre?
items.explanation: The grooves give water somewhere to go. More rubber touches the road, so there is enough friction to grip.

items.prompt: Which tool measures a force?
items.explanation: A forcemeter measures a force in newtons.

items.prompt: Which force pulls objects towards the ground?
items.explanation: Gravity is the pull of the Earth on everything.

items.prompt: Which force slows a bike when you use the brakes?
items.explanation: Brakes press on the wheel. The rubbing is friction and it slows the bike.

items.prompt: Which surface has the least friction?
items.explanation: Ice is very smooth, so there is little friction. That makes it slippery.

items.prompt: Why do we rub our hands to warm them?
hints: What force happens when surfaces rub?
items.explanation: When surfaces rub, friction changes movement energy into heat.

items.prompt: Which of these makes friction smaller?
items.explanation: Oil lets surfaces slide past each other more easily. This reduces friction.

items.prompt: A parachute opens. Which force pushes up against it?

options.why: The parachute is in the air.

hints: It is a type of friction.
items.explanation: Air resistance pushes up against the big canopy. This slows the fall.

items.prompt: Why are boats pointed at the front?
items.explanation: A pointed front moves through water more easily. It meets less resistance.

items.prompt: A heavy box is harder to push than a light box. Why?

options.text: There is more friction with the floor.

hints: Friction depends on how hard surfaces press.
items.explanation: A heavier box presses harder on the floor. That makes more friction.

items.prompt: Seena pushes a box with 10 N but it does not move. Why?

options.text: Friction pushes back with an equal force.

items.explanation: When the push is balanced by friction, the box stays still.

items.prompt: Is the friction useful or not wanted? Sort the cards.
items.explanation: Brakes, shoe grips and matches need friction. Machine parts rubbing, a wet floor and worn tyres are problems.

items.prompt: Is the surface smooth or rough? Sort the cards.
items.explanation: Ice, glass and polished tile are smooth. Sandpaper, grass and carpet are rough.

items.prompt: Choose all the ways to reduce friction.
items.explanation: Oil, wheels and smooth surfaces reduce friction. Sand and rough carpet increase it.

items.prompt: Choose all the forces.
hints: A force is a push or pull.
items.explanation: Gravity, friction and a push are forces. Light and sound are not forces.

items.prompt: Match each force to what it does.
items.explanation: Gravity pulls things to the Earth. Friction slows things that rub. Air and water resistance slow things moving through air or water.

items.prompt: Order the surfaces from the least to the most friction.
items.explanation: Ice has the least friction. Sandpaper has the most.

items.prompt: Friction is a force that acts when two surfaces ___. It ___ moving things.
items.explanation: Friction acts when two surfaces rub. It slows moving things.

items.prompt: Each rougher surface needs 2 N more. Fill in the table.
head: Surface
Force (N)
items.explanation: Add 2 N for each rougher surface: 1, 3, 5 and 7 N.

items.prompt: Raj pulls a toy box across three floors with a forcemeter. On tiles it reads 2 N. On carpet it reads 5 N. On a rubber mat it reads 8 N.

parts.prompt: Which floor has the most friction?
How many newtons more on the carpet than on the tiles?

hints: A bigger reading means more friction.
items.explanation: The rubber mat needs the biggest force, so it has the most friction. Carpet needs 5 - 2 = 3 N more than tiles.

items.prompt: A forcemeter reads 4 N on wood and 9 N on sandpaper. What is the difference?
hints: Subtract the smaller from the bigger.
items.explanation: 9 - 4 = 5 newtons.

items.prompt: Tap the rough surface.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: ice, sand, water and glass.

items.explanation: Sand is rough, so it has more friction than ice, water or glass.

items.prompt: The force of air pushing against a falling parachute is air ___.
items.explanation: Air resistance pushes up against a parachute and slows its fall.

items.prompt: Draw a shoe sole that grips well. Label the grip.

criteria.label: Draws a shoe sole with a pattern
Labels the grip and says why it helps

items.explanation: Grooves and bumps on a sole create friction with the ground, so we do not slip.

items.prompt: Three boxes are pushed over the same floor with the same push. Box A has 1 kg of sand. B has 3 kg. C has 2 kg. Which slides the shortest distance?
items.explanation: The heaviest box presses on the floor the most. There is more friction, so it slides the shortest distance.

items.prompt: A skater slides 10 m on ice. On sand she stops after 1 m. What does this show?

options.text: Sand has more friction than ice.
Ice has more friction than sand.

items.explanation: She stopped sooner on sand, so sand has more friction than ice.

items.prompt: A marble stops after 80, 30, 55 and 10 cm on four surfaces. Which surface has the most friction?

options.text: the one where it stopped at 10 cm
the one where it stopped at 80 cm
options.why: It went furthest, so friction was lowest.

options.text: the one where it stopped at 55 cm

items.explanation: The marble stopped soonest on that surface, so it has the most friction.
